headline: Canadian privacy regulators call for stronger governance of AI in health care and research
summary: Canada's federal, provincial and territorial privacy commissioners and ombuds passed a resolution urging responsible AI development, procurement and use in health care and health research, according to an October 29 release from the Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada. The release summarizes six principles and calls for legally required governance and accountability frameworks in health AI, updated research-ethics guidance and stronger ethics-board capacity. The full linked resolution could not be retrieved, and the recommendations are not evidence of enacted rules, institutional adoption or measured outcomes.
